chain.label: Incomplete guidance on monovision contact lens hazards
chain.trigger: incomplete guidance available to optometrists, aviation medical examiners, and pilots regarding the prescription of unapproved monovision contact lenses for use by pilots

chain.label: Captain's degraded depth perception from monovision contact lenses
chain.trigger: the captain's use of MV contact lenses resulted in his (unrecognized) degraded depth perception, and thus increased his dependence on monocular cues

caused_by.evidence: incomplete guidance available to optometrists, aviation medical examiners, and pilots regarding the prescription of unapproved monovision contact lenses

chain.label: Low ceiling, heavy rain/fog, featureless water approach
chain.trigger: low clouds, moderate-to-heavy rain and fog...the airplane was positioned over the waters of Flushing Bay (which appeared gray), with no visible structures to aid in visually judging distance and/or altitude

chain.label: Irregular runway 13 edge light spacing
chain.trigger: the runway lights were installed at irregular intervals...the most common distances between lights falling between 120 feet and 170 feet

chain.label: Captain's misperception of airplane's position relative to runway
chain.trigger: the inability of the captain, because of his use of monovision contact lenses, to overcome his misperception of the airplane's position relative to the runway during the visual portion of the approach

caused_by.evidence: the inability of the captain, because of his use of monovision contact lenses, to overcome his misperception
visual illusions produced by the approach over water in limited light conditions, the absence of visible ground features, the rain and fog
the irregular spacing of the runway lights

chain.label: Non-instantaneous VSI displayed misleading descent rate
chain.trigger: as the first officer called out a sink rate of 700 feet per minute...the airplane was actually descending about 1,200 feet per minute...the lag time in the non-instantaneous vertical speed information

chain.label: Uncommanded steepening of descent below glidepath in final seconds
chain.trigger: the airplane's rate of descent increased...to about 1,800 feet per minute...his unnecessarily steepening the approach during the final 10 seconds before impact

caused_by.evidence: led the captain to perceive that the airplane was higher than it was...and thus, to his unnecessarily steepening the approach during the final 10 seconds before impact

the difference between the 700 feet per minute rate of descent reported...and the 1,200 feet per minute rate of descent indicated by the FDR data was probably the result of the lag time in the non-instantaneous vertical speed information

chain.label: Collision with approach light structure and runway deck
chain.trigger: the airplane struck the approach light structure and the vertical edge of the concrete runway deck

caused_by.evidence: the airplane struck the approach light structure and the vertical edge of the concrete runway deck
